central_question: What incremental reserved public cash can Arkansas earn from cooperative/community food-hub ownership and in-state processing margins, and can we trace an Arkansas dollar through that pathway under normal conditions and a serious economic shock?
hard_wall: Farm cash receipts ≠ processing margins ≠ public revenue.

lane_discipline.main: Food-hub evidence → retained value → reserved cash → Replacement Stack
lane_discipline.resilience: First concrete test object for five-state framework — does not open a resilience implementation slice

count_rule: COUNTABLE NOW requires evidence-backed incremental reserved cash. Illustrative EICR and dollar traces are not countable.

effect_on_pathway: Farm-gate dollars shrink → hub throughput and lease capacity weaken

resilience_first_object.lesson: Resilience testing starts by stressing a real dollar path — not by inventing a resilience revenue engine

replacement_stack_feed.rule: Feed only defensible dollars — none this slice

headline.reading: Arkansas farm-gate scale is large (~$13.1B cash receipts). That still does not retire taxes. Processing ownership and reserved cash remain unproven. Dollar-trace shows why local hub ownership matters for retention — and why recession stress makes ownership design more, not less, important. COUNTABLE $0.
